decisions.executionNote: Begin left elbow-up approach to the rear-left tube; raise and tilt the open gripper before advancing. Tube geometry estimated from calibrated head view.
Advance the left open gripper above the rear-left tube while maintaining the elbow-up arc and completing most of the downward grasp tilt.
Center on the rear-left tube and lower to grasp height, using small steps to finish aligning the fingers across its body.
Fine-center using wrist view, shift slightly toward the cap, then close the left gripper around the tube body.
Lift the closed left gripper clear of the table; check that the tube remains between the fingers before turning upright.
Tube remains visibly retained. Turn it toward upright while carrying it toward the rack center, with conservative rotation increments.
Continue upright rotation and position above a central rack slot; keep the tube elevated while aligning.
Finish the upright orientation and refine slot alignment using the observed tube position; begin a shallow descent only.
Use the upright tube silhouette to correct slightly left and toward the robot, then lower slowly toward the central front slot.
Lower the aligned upright tube the final four centimeters into the rack, holding it closed until the seated position can be checked.
Open to release the seated first tube and retract left clear of the rack. Begin an elbow-up right-arm approach to the right-side tube.
First tube is standing released in the rack. Retract left toward home while advancing the open right gripper above its tube and completing the downward tilt.
Align the right fingers across the tube body and descend nearly to grasp height; continue the left arm's smooth elbow-up return.
Fine-center the right tube in the wrist view, adjust yaw and grasp height, then close. Finish returning the empty left arm to its origin.
Lift the right tube with the gripper held closed, keeping it in the right workspace and checking retention before reorientation.
Right tube is retained. Begin slowly rotating it upright above the right side of the rack, preserving the elbow-up branch.
Continue turning the retained right tube upright with small increments while approaching the rightmost front rack slot.
Finish the right tube's upright rotation above its slot, maintaining clearance until alignment is visible.
Refine rightmost-slot alignment from the upright tube silhouette and descend slowly, keeping the right gripper closed.
Lower the upright right tube into the rightmost front slot to the seated height; keep the gripper closed until the next visual check.
Release the second tube and withdraw right clear of the rack. Start an elbow-up left approach to the final tube, matching its different tabletop angle.
Both released tubes are upright in the rack. Advance left above the remaining tube while tilting across its axis; return the empty right arm along an elbow-up arc.
Finish the final tube's downward grasp alignment and lower near its body; ease the empty right arm toward origin without changing elbow branch.
Use the wrist view to refine the final tube's yaw and grasp depth, then close the left gripper; settle the right arm at origin.
Lift the final tube clear with the left gripper closed, checking that it stays retained before rotating upright.
Carry the retained final tube toward the leftmost open slot and begin its upright rotation, preserving clearance and elbow-up continuity.
Continue the smooth upright turn and left-slot approach, keeping the final tube retained and above the rack.
Complete the upright turn above the leftmost free slot, then use the head and wrist views to refine the final insertion alignment.
Refine leftmost-slot alignment and gently compensate the final tube's apparent backward lean while approaching above the opening.
Make a small final planar correction and lower the retained tube into the leftmost opening, monitoring seating before release.
Complete the final shallow insertion, then open the left gripper while holding position so the tube can settle into the rack.
All three tubes appear seated and released. Withdraw the open left gripper clear before returning both arms to their starting poses.
The three tubes remain upright without gripper support. Continue the empty left arm's elbow-up return and restore both wrists toward their origin orientations.
